There he looked after many war orphans and taught them. His experiences in Stans became important for his ideas on education. Pestalozzi is now regarded as one of the best-known educators in Switzerland.

gewusst: In Nidwalden the events are still called the “French invasion” (Franzosenüberfall) to this day.
This term became well known in 1862 through a book by Franz Joseph Gut.

teile.einleitung: The **Savoy Affair** was a dispute in 1860 over the region of northern Savoy south of Lake Geneva. When France took over Savoy, Switzerland feared for its security and for Geneva. The dispute brought Switzerland to the brink of a conflict with France.
wichtigste: Since the Congress of Vienna, Switzerland had been allowed to occupy Chablais and Faucigny in the event of war.
In 1860 Sardinia-Piedmont ceded Savoy and Nice to France in the Treaty of Turin.
Federal Councillor Jakob Stämpfli demanded a military occupation of northern Savoy.
Parliament wanted to carry on negotiating first.
The people of northern Savoy voted for France with “oui et zone”.
The dispute over the free zones went before an international court in 1932.

abschnitte.text: After the **Congress of Vienna** of 1815 Savoy belonged to the **Kingdom of Sardinia-Piedmont**. The northern provinces of **Chablais** and **Faucigny** were neutralised. To protect its **neutrality**, Switzerland was allowed to occupy them militarily in the event of war. The area lies right next to Geneva and was important for Switzerland.

France had helped Sardinia-Piedmont in the war against Austria. In return King **Victor Emmanuel II** ceded Savoy and Nice to **France** on **24 March 1860** in the **Treaty of Turin**. Switzerland now feared that Geneva might be enclosed by France. It hoped to get at least northern Savoy.

Federal Councillor **Jakob Stämpfli**, a Bernese radical, distrusted the French promises. He demanded that northern Savoy be occupied militarily. But Parliament followed **Alfred Escher** and **Jakob Dubs**. The Federal Assembly justified its refusal by saying that diplomatic means had not yet been exhausted. At the end of March 1860 about 150 **volunteer irregulars** from Geneva and Savoy seized a steamship and landed on the Savoy shore. Regular Swiss troops quickly brought them back.

In April 1860 the men of Savoy voted on joining France. The people of northern Savoy were promised a **free trade zone** with Switzerland. So they voted by a majority **“oui et zone”**, that is, yes to France and to the zone. For Switzerland this was a failure. The President of the Confederation, **Friedrich Frey-Herosé**, was re-elected only narrowly in autumn 1860.

abschnitte.titel: The long dispute over the zones
abschnitte.text: In 1919 France wanted to abolish the **free zones**. The dispute went before the **Permanent Court of International Justice** in **The Hague**. In 1932 the court decided that France was not allowed simply to abolish the zones. So the Savoy question remained an issue for over 70 years.

gewusst: Nice, which also went to France in 1860, was the home town of the Italian freedom fighter Giuseppe Garibaldi.
The irregulars of 1860 acted without the permission of the Federal Council.

teile.einleitung: Watchmaking is an old craft for which Switzerland is world famous. Especially in the Jura fine watches have been made for centuries. It takes a lot of patience, steady hands and good light.
wichtigste: Watchmaking is especially at home in the Jura.
In the past farmers made watch parts in winter.
According to legend Daniel JeanRichard repaired an English watch.
Watchmakers need a magnifying glass for the tiny parts.
La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle have been UNESCO World Heritage since 2009.
The watchmaking craft has been intangible cultural heritage of UNESCO since 2020.

abschnitte.text: The **Jura** is a mountain range in the north west of Switzerland. Since the 18th century many watch workshops arose there. In the long winter there was little work on the farms. So many **farming families** made watch parts in their living rooms. In this way they earned extra money. To this day there are famous watch firms in the Jura.

A well known legend tells of **Daniel JeanRichard**. As a teenager he is said to have repaired a broken watch from England. After that he made watches himself and trained **apprentices**. In this way the craft is said to have spread in the Jura. Whether everything happened exactly like that is not known for sure.

The parts of a watch are often smaller than a grain of rice. So a watchmaker needs a **magnifying glass**. With it he sees the tiny wheels and screws large. A lot of **daylight** is also important. In **La Chaux-de-Fonds** the houses therefore have many big windows. In the town's **International Watchmaking Museum** you can marvel at thousands of watches from many centuries.

The towns of **La Chaux-de-Fonds** and **Le Locle** were built entirely for the watchmakers. Since **2009** they have belonged to the **UNESCO World Heritage**. In **2020** UNESCO also took the watchmaking craft of Switzerland and France into the **intangible cultural heritage**. What is meant by this is the knowledge and skill of the people. In the **Vallée de Joux** in the Vaud Jura especially complicated watches are made.

gewusst: The International Watchmaking Museum in La Chaux-de-Fonds is one of the biggest watch museums in the world.
Some watches from the Vallée de Joux show not only the time but also moon phases and a calendar.
